item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, these catalytic domains share the Actin-like ATPase domain superfamily c.55.1 (SUNID 53067), within the Ribonuclease H-like motif fold c.55 and alpha/beta class c. They remain distinct families: Actin/HSP70 is c.55.1.1 (SUNID 53068), hexokinase is c.55.1.3 (SUNID 53083), and glycerol kinase is c.55.1.4 (SUNID 53089). Thus actin and HSP70 have the stronger family-level relationship, whereas their relationship to hexokinase and glycerol kinase is only at superfamily level. This supports probable remote homology—a common ancestral catalytic-domain architecture—and permits cautious inference of a conserved ATP-linked structural/mechanistic core. It does not justify transferring substrate specificity, exact reaction, kinetics, regulation, cellular role, individual catalytic residues, domain boundaries, or whole-protein homology. A member may serve as a remote structural template for the domain core, but family-matched representatives should be preferred and any transfer requires target-specific sequence/structure alignment, active-site conservation, and biochemical evidence; a SCOPe representative is not automatically equivalent to the target.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop — /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=hexokinase&mode=auto&limit=50; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=glycerol+kinase&mode=auto&limit=50","mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53083; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53083/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53089; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53089/parents","Pretrained model knowledge — interpretation of SCOPe hierarchy and limits on homology, function transfer, and template use"]}]}
